tests.name: test_good_calls
tests.description: Calls that keep the contract work as before: 10 halvings from 1.0 to 0.001, 14 steps of 0.9 from 4.0 to 1.0, and none when the start is already low enough.

tests.name: test_target
tests.description: A target of 0, or below 0, stops the call with AssertionError.

tests.name: test_factor
tests.description: A factor of 0 or below, or of 1 or above, stops the call with AssertionError.
tests.message: steps_to(0.001, 1.0, -0.5) gives 1 instead of stopping with AssertionError, though its factor is not between 0 and 1.

tests.name: test_messages
tests.description: Each message names the parameter at fault: the one for a bad target says target, the one for a bad factor says factor, and the two are not the same.

tests.name: test_filled
tests.description: first_bad gives a step, not None.

tests.name: test_million
tests.description: Between 0 and 1,000,000, with the first bad step at 637,000, it gives 637,000, asking is_bad at most 20 times.
tests.message: first_bad has asked is_bad 21 times, more than the 20 that halving needs here.

tests.name: test_trillion
tests.description: Between 0 and 10**12, a million million, with the first bad step at 777,777,777,777, it gives that step, asking is_bad at most 40 times.
tests.message: first_bad has asked is_bad 41 times, more than the 40 that halving needs here.

tests.name: test_anywhere
tests.description: Between 0 and 64, it finds the first bad step wherever it is, from 1 to 64, asking at most 6 times.
tests.message: first_bad has asked is_bad 7 times, more than the 6 that halving needs here.

tests.name: test_next_to_each_other
tests.description: When hi is lo + 1, hi is the first bad step, and no check is needed.
tests.message: first_bad has asked is_bad 1 time, more than the 0 that halving needs here.

tests.name: test_whole_number
tests.description: It gives a whole number, an int, as step numbers are.

tests.name: test_examples
tests.description: Steps 0, 9, 10 and 25 of the schedule in the task have the rates 0.1, 0.1, 0.05 and 0.025.

tests.name: test_first_change
tests.description: With every set to 4, the rate is still the start at step 3 and first changes at step 4.
tests.message: lr_at(1, 1.0, 0.5, 4) gives 0.5, not 1.0: the rate should first change at step 4.

tests.name: test_compounds
tests.description: Each change multiplies the rate reached so far, so three changes of 0.9 from 0.1 give 0.1 × 0.9 × 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.0729.

tests.name: test_every_step
tests.description: With every set to 1, the rate changes at every step, so step 3 has 1.0 × 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.125.
